blueprints.primary_construct: Track one speaker's concern and identify how the second speaker responds
blueprints.prompt_text: Listen once without reading the transcript. Then explain: (1) why Mia is unsure about the workshop, and (2) what Leo's response is trying to help her do.

material.transcript_text: Mia: I know the optional research workshop could help, but it meets on Friday afternoon, when I usually finish my lab reports. I am not sure the benefit is worth losing that time. Leo: That makes sense. Why not attend the first meeting and ask whether later sessions are recorded? Then you can judge the value without committing every Friday.

criteria.description: Identifies the time conflict and Mia's uncertainty about whether the benefit is worth it
Explains that Leo validates the concern and proposes a trial before commitment

required_meaning_units: Friday workshop conflicts with lab-report time
Mia is unsure about the tradeoff
Leo proposes attending once and checking recordings before deciding
semantic_scope.acceptable_variants: Any wording that preserves the concern-response relationship
invalid_conditions: states only isolated details without the relationship

blueprints.primary_construct: Give a clear strategy explanation with an ordered process and reason
blueprints.prompt_text: A classmate understands lectures but forgets the content a few days later. Recommend one study strategy. Explain what to do first, what to do next, and why the strategy should help. Speak for about 45 seconds.

criteria.description: Explains at least two steps in a clear order
Connects the strategy to remembering content

semantic_scope.acceptable_variants: Any realistic strategy with a coherent explanation

blueprints.primary_construct: Identify an expository text's main line and explain how a detail supports it
blueprints.prompt_text: Read the passage. State its main organizational line, then explain how the detail about attendance after week four supports the writer's conclusion.

material.text: Last semester, Northbridge University tested optional peer-led review sessions in three introductory courses. The sessions were designed to solve a common problem: students often waited until the week before an exam to discover what they did not understand. During each meeting, a trained student leader asked participants to explain one difficult idea, compare two possible solutions, and write down one question to take to the instructor. Early attendance was high, but it fell after the fourth week, especially in the course whose instructor rarely referred to the sessions. In the other two courses, instructors used anonymous questions from the meetings in later lectures, and attendance remained steadier. Exam results alone could not prove that the sessions caused better learning, because students chose whether to attend. However, the pilot suggested that peer review works best when it is connected visibly to the main course rather than offered as a separate extra service.

criteria.description: Explains that contrasting attendance patterns support the value of visible course connection

required_meaning_units: pilot addressed delayed recognition of confusion
conclusion is qualified rather than causal
semantic_scope.acceptable_variants: Any accurate description of the same organizational and evidential relationship
invalid_conditions: claims the exam results proved causation

blueprints.primary_construct: Write a short explanation with a clear recommendation, process, and sentence boundaries
blueprints.prompt_text: In about 80 words, explain one practical way a university student can reduce phone distractions while studying. State the method, explain how to use it, and give one reason it should work.

criteria.description: States one practical method for reducing phone distraction
Explains how to use the method and why it should work
Uses understandable sentence boundaries and links the ideas clearly

semantic_scope.acceptable_variants: Any safe and realistic method that answers the task
invalid_conditions: only names a method without explaining it

blueprints.primary_construct: Transfer a beginning-development-ending explanation to a new problem-solving context
blueprints.prompt_text: A campus project group has missed two deadlines because members wait for someone else to organize the work. Recommend one change. Explain how the group should begin, what should happen during the week, and what result you expect. Speak for 45–60 seconds.

criteria.description: Organizes the response as beginning, development, and expected ending
Connects the change to the missed-deadline problem

semantic_scope.acceptable_variants: Any realistic group-process solution with a coherent sequence

blueprints.primary_construct: Review C0004 evidence, decide the focus goal, and confirm the next cycle before writing it
blueprints.prompt_text: Use the bounded C0004 evidence packet to present the focus-goal result, maintenance coverage, unresolved uncertainty, and one recommended next-cycle focus with an alternative. Ask for confirmation before changing the plan.
